projects.name: Themis
projects.title: Better evaluations. A fraction of the cost.
projects.summary: A hybrid agentic grader combining deterministic checks, structured rubrics, and model judgement to benchmark AI-generated spreadsheets and presentations.
projects.challenge: Evaluating model-generated artefacts needs more than a plausible-sounding answer. The grader has to assess correctness against expected outputs and explicit criteria, while keeping repeated benchmarking affordable and reproducible.
approach: Designed and implemented Themis as a hybrid grading pipeline: deterministic validation for machine-checkable properties, rubric-based assessment, and LLM judgement for the remaining criteria.
Built custom evaluation environments that execute grading workflows end to end and compare model outputs with golden datasets and structured rubrics.
Automated repeatable benchmarking across multiple models and compared the approach with Gandalf the Grader and LLM-as-a-Judge methods.
projects.decision: Different criteria need different graders. Combining deterministic checks with rubric-guided model assessment creates a clearer boundary between what can be verified directly and what requires judgement.
projects.scope: Results are reported in my resume for the evaluation workflows used at Aptura. They describe that benchmark context; they are not a general claim about model accuracy. This case study summarises my contribution without publishing employer code or datasets.
projects.reflection: Evaluation is part of the engineering system. Cost, reproducibility, and the ability to explain a score matter alongside the score itself.

projects.name: Billacord
projects.title: From contract terms to billing evidence.
projects.summary: A contract-to-invoice checking product with source-backed term review, deterministic calculations, separate client workspaces, and exportable evidence.
projects.challenge: Negotiated terms, amendments, discounts, and renewal increases can drift from what is billed. A useful finance tool must show the source of a finding and its calculation, and distinguish a potential difference from a confirmed error or recovered payment.
approach: Built a local Node.js application with owner and client logins, separate ledgers, invitations, membership revocation, and workspace-specific reports.

Added document and invoice imports, a replaceable AI extraction provider, and manual term entry. Reviewers see exact supporting excerpts beside proposed terms and approve them before checking invoices.
Implemented deterministic comparison of approved terms and before-tax invoice amounts, including multiple charges, supported seat-based pricing, and monthly, quarterly, and annual periods.

Built findings review, renewal tracking, billing setup sheets, and PDF, CSV, and HTML evidence exports. Potential differences, confirmed errors, corrections, and collected cash retain distinct statuses.
projects.decision: Use the model to propose structured terms, then make approval and arithmetic explicit. The billing checker runs against approved data, making a finding traceable to both contract evidence and a reproducible calculation.
projects.scope: A private local MVP with synthetic verification and a separate evaluation dataset. Customer demand and commercial outcomes remain unvalidated. Live extraction accuracy has not yet been established by the planned independent baseline. Billacord is the current working name; older folders use ClauseTally or ReplyLedger.
projects.reflection: Finance reviewers need evidence they can inspect. Treating extraction, approval, calculation, and resolution as separate stages makes the product easier to audit and improve.

projects.name: ActionProof
projects.title: Did the agent do only what was approved?
projects.summary: A TypeScript verifier that checks approval boundaries against actual state changes and keeps missing evidence visible.
projects.challenge: An allowed decision does not prove that an action was correct. Approval can refer to the wrong target, cross an account boundary, or become unverifiable when post-execution evidence is unavailable.
approach: Built a dependency-free TypeScript demonstration around a synthetic ticket store, with deliberately broken and corrected reference controls.
Ran five isolated scenarios covering an approved action, missing approval, a changed ticket target, customer separation, and unavailable post-execution evidence.
Compared before-and-after state with the authorised action and produced a self-contained HTML and JSON report with explicit pass, fail, and inconclusive results.
projects.decision: Verify the observable effect, not just the control's returned decision. Missing state evidence remains inconclusive, so a successful function return cannot silently become a security pass.
results: Broken control changes the wrong ticket
projects.scope: This verifies our own synthetic reference example. It is a local demonstration, not a production security product or a customer vulnerability finding. Real identity, transport, concurrency, expiry, and customer-system adapters require separate work.
projects.reflection: A useful verifier must be willing to say it cannot conclude. Keeping uncertainty visible is as important as detecting a seeded failure.

projects.name: Financial document QA
projects.title: Model reasoning. Verified arithmetic.
projects.summary: A conversational financial QA pipeline with structured model output, restricted expression execution, and resumable evaluation on ConvFinQA.
projects.challenge: Financial questions combine language understanding with precise calculation. Follow-up questions also depend on earlier answers, so a single-turn score can conceal errors across a conversation.
approach: Built a CLI pipeline that loads a financial record, preserves question-and-answer history, and requests a structured response validated with Pydantic.
Separated model reasoning from arithmetic with a restricted Python expression interpreter that blocks imports, function calls, and arbitrary code execution.
Added interchangeable OpenAI and Gemini adapters, explicit abstention, and resumable JSONL evaluation using seeded sampling.
Reported strict turn accuracy, disclosed percentage-normalised accuracy, and conversation accuracy separately. Supported both gold and predicted conversation history.
projects.decision: The model selects values and operations; deterministic code computes the numerical answer. For the supplied small records, full-document context avoided adding retrieval errors to the first baseline.
projects.scope: The recorded Gemini live run covers four development conversations and fourteen turns with seed 42 and gold history. It is a prototype smoke test, not a stable benchmark estimate. Evidence quotes are not yet verified against source text, and this run does not measure predicted-history error propagation. The project report records 82 passing tests and 87% source coverage at that verification point.
projects.reflection: Disclose the denominator and history setting with every accuracy number. A high turn score can coexist with weak whole-conversation performance.

projects.name: TampStamp
projects.title: A loyalty loop for independent cafés.
projects.summary: A digital stamp and coffee-gifting platform with rotating QR codes, database-enforced access rules, and a vendor portal.
projects.challenge: Replacing paper loyalty cards needs a fast customer experience and controls that vendors can rely on. Stamps must be tied to the right café and user, and a QR scan must not create repeated rewards.
approach: Built customer and vendor journeys with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Supabase authentication, Postgres, and row-level security.
Implemented short-lived rotating QR sessions and database functions for stamp issuance and reward redemption. A uniqueness constraint limits each customer card to one stamp per QR rotation.
Added vendor onboarding, guarded café management, loyalty programme editing, and a portal displaying customers, stamps, and redemptions.
Built a Stripe Checkout coffee-gifting flow with addressed and shareable gifts, vendor redemption, and reimbursement tracking.
projects.decision: Enforce the loyalty rules in database functions and constraints. The customer interface initiates a scan; the database validates the token, ownership, expiry, and duplicate-stamp condition.
projects.scope: A private product build. The repository documents implemented loyalty, vendor, and gifting flows; this portfolio does not claim a public launch, adoption, or revenue. Paid loyalty upgrades remain separate from the implemented gifting checkout, and app-store release requires further work.
projects.reflection: The simplest customer interaction can have a substantial system behind it. Put the invariant where every client has to obey it.

projects.name: Enterprise AI governance
projects.title: Making governance part of the workflow.
projects.summary: An enterprise pilot translating policy and risk criteria into structured inputs, approval gates, and traceable lifecycle decisions.
projects.challenge: Governance policies describe requirements, but delivery systems still need an interpretable way to decide what can happen next. In the Nationwide pilot, the work was to turn risk and compliance intent into structured workflow constraints.
approach: Defined metadata schemas and risk-tier inputs, separating customer impact from data sensitivity so reviewers could understand what triggered a control.
Mapped risk tiers to conditional workflow paths, mandatory evidence, and approval checkpoints, with state transitions that constrained lifecycle progression.
Worked across orchestration and enterprise content services, including watsonx, MCP interfaces, FileNet on OpenShift, and supporting metadata and artefact storage.
projects.decision: Keep the rule and the rationale connected. A reviewer should be able to trace a required control back to the structured input that triggered it, with proportionate requirements for lower-risk paths.
projects.scope: This is a qualitative pilot case study based on the existing public portfolio account. It describes engineering contributions and the integration approach, not an independent compliance certification or a quantified customer outcome.
projects.reflection: Governance becomes useful to engineering teams when policy is expressed as clear inputs, enforceable transitions, and evidence they can inspect.
